blocks.html: Brand Equity refers to the intangible value a brand holds in the marketplace, shaped by customer perceptions, recognition, trust, and overall reputation.

Brand equity represents how strongly a brand resonates with its audience and influences purchasing decisions. A brand with high equity is more likely to attract, retain, and command loyalty from customers, often allowing it to differentiate itself and justify premium pricing.
Brand equity is built over time through consistent customer experiences and strategic brand-building efforts, including:

items.html: Trust and credibility in the market
Emotional connection with the target audience

blocks.html: Supports premium pricing and higher margins
These factors collectively influence how customers perceive and choose a brand over competitors.

A well-established software company with a strong reputation for reliability and customer support is often preferred over lesser-known competitors, even at a higher price point—demonstrating strong brand equity.

Brand equity is a critical asset that reflects the strength of a brand in the minds of customers. Businesses that invest in building trust, consistency, and positive experiences can create lasting value and influence buying decisions.
